products.name: Canary
products.tagline: The all-rounder witness — full sensing plus the Home Assistant bridge.

hatch.title: Your Canary is on its perch.
hatch.body: The magical first proof is local and physical: join its setup network, open the dashboard, then make one harmless signal it can witness.

products.name: Canary Vision
products.tagline: Person detection on the camera module itself — only “someone is here” ever leaves the board.
products.provisioning_note: This sensor learns your WiFi from the firmware you flash. The signed release carries safe placeholders; to bake in your own network, build it once with your secrets (the guide shows how) — every later update inherits it from the device’s memory.

hatch.title: Your Vision Canary is waking up.
hatch.body: Give it one visible, privacy-safe thing to notice immediately: presence only, no faces and no saved frames.
steps: If you have not flashed the Grove Vision AI V2 module yet, move the USB-C cable to the module port and flash the pinned model.
Put the board where it can see a doorway, then walk through once.
Open Home Assistant and watch the presence entity flip to detected, then clear.

presets.title: As it ships
presets.blurb: The firmware’s own defaults — balanced for a first bring-up. Pick nothing and this is what you get.

presets.title: Entryway / front door
presets.blurb: Presence at the door is the event; nobody dwells in a doorway. Fast lost timeout, short dwell — the voxel column tells you in/out of the frame.

presets.title: Living room / shared space
presets.blurb: Occupancy is the question, not motion. Longer lost timeout rides through stillness (reading, TV); dwelling becomes the useful signal.

presets.title: Hallway / corridor
presets.blurb: People transit fast — a low dwell would never latch anyway. Default score, snappy lost timeout, dwell long so a lingerer stands out.

presets.title: Garage / workshop
presets.blurb: Harsh light and clutter: raise the score floor to shrug off shadows and shapes; dwell marks a real work session.

presets.title: Home office
presets.blurb: A monitor is in frame by definition — raise the threshold, trust dwell. Screen-people flicker below it; you at the desk persist above it.

erase_all.label: Erase the entire chip first
erase_all.what: Wipes every byte — firmware, settings, stored WiFi, witness history — then writes fresh. A factory reset and an install in one pass.
erase_all.when: A board that misbehaves in ways an ordinary reinstall doesn’t fix, or one you’re handing to someone else.
erase_all.default: Off — a normal install only touches the regions the new firmware needs.

skip_backup.label: Skip the automatic safety copy
skip_backup.what: Normally every byte on the board is saved to your downloads before anything is written — that file is your undo button.
skip_backup.when: Only when you already backed this exact board up this session and want to save the minute.
skip_backup.default: Off — the copy happens by itself.

wifi_bake.label: WiFi at install time
wifi_bake.what: Typed here, your network is written into the chip’s settings region in the same pass as the firmware — the Canary joins it on first boot. It never leaves this page except over the USB cable.
wifi_bake.when: Always worth it if you know the network; leave it empty and the board raises its own setup WiFi instead.
wifi_bake.default: Empty — the setup network is the fallback either way.

local_file.label: Install a local file
local_file.what: Flashes a .bin you built or downloaded yourself. Signatures can’t be checked for a personal file, but the write is still verified against the chip and the board still can’t be bricked.
local_file.when: Your own builds, air-gapped setups, or restoring someone’s shared image.

restore_backup.label: Restore a backup
restore_backup.what: Rewinds the board to the exact moment a backup file was taken — firmware, settings, identity, everything.
restore_backup.when: After an experiment, a downgrade gone odd, or to clone a known-good state back onto the same board.

dev_channel.label: Dev channel
dev_channel.what: ?channel=dev in the address bar switches to the rolling prerelease — signed with the same key, newer, less soaked.
dev_channel.when: You’re testing a fix the maintainer just cut. Remove the parameter to return to stable.

flash_speed.label: Flash speed
flash_speed.what: How fast bytes move over USB (921600 baud first). The flasher steps down by itself when a cable can’t keep up — speed never costs correctness, every byte is verified after.
flash_speed.default: Automatic — no setting to get wrong.

det_score.label: Confidence floor
det_score.what: How sure the camera must be before “someone is here” counts (0–100). Higher shrugs off shadows and screen-people; lower catches more at the cost of false alarms.
det_score.when: Raise it in rooms with monitors or glare; lower it if real people go unnoticed.

det_lost.label: Lost timeout
det_lost.what: How long with no person in frame before presence flips back to “clear”. Short feels snappy; long rides through someone sitting still.
det_lost.when: Short for doorways and hallways, long for sofas and desks.

det_dwell.label: Dwell threshold
det_dwell.what: How long someone must stay before it counts as dwelling — the difference between passing through and being there.
det_dwell.when: Short where any stop matters (an entryway), long where lingering is the signal (a hallway at night).

det_target.label: What it looks for
det_target.what: The model class treated as “person”. With the pinned person-detection model this stays 0 — it exists so a future model swap can’t strand the firmware.
det_target.when: Only with a custom model whose person class sits elsewhere.

tscore.label: Module confidence (TSCORE)
tscore.what: The camera module’s own reporting floor — below it, the module doesn’t even mention a box. Lives on the module, set over the bench wire, separate from the firmware’s confidence floor.

tiou.label: Module overlap (TIOU)
tiou.what: How much two candidate boxes may overlap before the module merges them into one person instead of reporting two.

sense_flavor.label: Which Sense build
sense_flavor.what: Canary Sense watches presence only. Sense · Wellbeing adds breathing and heart-rate sensing — a genuinely different privacy surface, which is why it’s a separate firmware, not a toggle.
sense_flavor.when: Wellbeing only where vitals are wanted (a bedside); presence-only everywhere else.

present_debounce_ms.label: Presence debounce
present_debounce_ms.what: How long the radar must keep seeing a target before “someone is here” is announced — the guard against blinks and noise.

clear_timeout_ms.label: Clear timeout
clear_timeout_ms.what: How long with no target before the room reads empty again.

stall_timeout_ms.label: Radar stall alarm
stall_timeout_ms.what: No frames at all from the radar for this long means the sensor link itself is in trouble — state becomes “unknown”, never a silent guess.

range_near_cm.label: Near band
range_near_cm.what: Inside this distance counts as “near”. Only the coarse band ever leaves the device — raw centimetres stay on the board.

range_mid_cm.label: Mid band
range_mid_cm.what: Between near and this is “mid”; beyond it, “far”. Three honest buckets instead of a tracking dot.

vitals_lock_ms.label: Vitals lock
vitals_lock_ms.what: Breathing must hold steady this long before the Wellbeing build trusts it — and vitals are suppressed entirely unless exactly one person is in view.

vitals_lost_ms.label: Vitals lost
vitals_lost_ms.what: How long without a plausible breathing signal before the lock is dropped rather than guessed at.

display_emulator.label: The 1:1 emulator
display_emulator.what: The real display firmware — same C++, same LVGL — compiled to run in the browser. The pixels you see are the pixels the glass will show, framebuffer out, touch in. It boots on the fleet page; the flasher itself runs a stricter security policy on purpose.
display_emulator.when: Before building a Watch Station or Dash: try the face, the touch, the night floor, without hardware.

we2_module.name: Grove Vision AI V2 — the Vision’s camera module
we2_module.chip: Himax HX6538 (WiseEye2) · Ethos-U55 NPU · CH343 USB-serial

model.name: Person Detection
model.arch: Swift-YOLO (tiny) · 192×192×3 RGB · compiled for the Ethos-U55
model.license: MIT — Seeed SSCMA model zoo, redistributable with attribution
model.why_pinned: One model, chosen and tested with the canary-vision firmware train. No catalog to scroll, no wrong pick to make — and the firmware’s runtime class-index setting absorbs any future swap.

we2_module.port_note: the MODULE’s USB-C port (the big carrier-PCB one, next to the Grove connector) — not the XIAO’s. The XIAO port cannot reach the Himax flash.
we2_module.persistence: The model lives in the module’s own 16 MB flash and persists across power cycles and every future host reflash.
we2_module.no_brick: The burn menu lives in the HX6538’s ROM bootloader — an interrupted transfer just means reset and flash again. And a bricked module bootloader is still recoverable through the host over I2C (we2_iic_bootloader_recover — device guide §7).
we2_module.engine: SecuraCV WE2 engine (assets/we2-core.js) — XMODEM/CRC-16 at 921600 over WebSerial, the same wire protocol Seeed’s open-source flasher speaks, clean-room implemented and pinned by tests/we2.test.js.

steps: Plug the MODULE’s own USB-C port into this computer — the big port on the camera carrier board, next to the Grove connector. The XIAO’s port can’t reach the camera.
Click Connect and pick “USB Single Serial” (the CH343). If the model isn’t on the module yet, burn it first — one click, verified.
Press “Start live preview”. Frames appear within a second or two, with a box and a confidence score on everything the model finds.
Aim and light it like the real spot: face the camera, two to four meters, light on you rather than behind you. Watch the meter climb.
Tune if needed: Confidence (TSCORE) is the module’s reporting floor — raise it to shrug off weak phantoms, lower it to catch more. IoU (TIOU) merges overlapping boxes of the same object.
Press Stop when done. Day-to-day aiming stays boxes-only over MQTT — the video stream exists only on this attended bench.

troubleshooting.when: No port shows up in the picker
troubleshooting.fix: Wrong port (the XIAO’s instead of the module’s), a charge-only cable, or Linux missing the one udev rule — device guide §7. Unplug, replug into the module’s port, use a data cable.

troubleshooting.when: Connected, but Start shows no frames
troubleshooting.fix: The module may still be in its bootloader — power-cycle it (unplug/replug), reconnect, start again. If it persists, the module might run non-SSCMA firmware; reflash the model here.
Check the model is burned (the header above says so), then step back — Swift-YOLO wants the whole person in frame, not a face filling it. Try more light, or lower Confidence a notch.

troubleshooting.when: The image is black or very dark
troubleshooting.fix: Peel the lens film if it’s still on, add light in front of the camera, and give the sensor a second to auto-expose.

troubleshooting.when: Boxes flicker or split in two
troubleshooting.fix: Raise IoU (TIOU) slightly so overlapping candidates merge, or raise Confidence so marginal duplicates drop.
Confidence is a reporting floor, not a grade — a steady 60-80% on a well-lit person is normal and plenty. Chase framing and light before chasing 99%.

no_brick.headline: You cannot brick your Canary from here.
no_brick.why: The ESP32’s first-stage bootloader lives in mask ROM — it can’t be erased or overwritten over USB. If a flash is interrupted or an image is wrong, the board just drops back into download mode and you flash again. Nothing you click here is one-way.
points: Unplug mid-flash? No harm — reconnect and start over.
Wrong image for the chip? The flasher won’t offer it, and the ROM would refuse it anyway.
Want to go back? Take a one-click backup first and restore it any time.

recovery.when: The board doesn’t show up when you click Connect
recovery.do: Unplug and replug the USB-C cable — use a data cable, not a charge-only one. Then click Connect again.

recovery.when: It connects but won’t sync / detect
recovery.do: Put it in download mode by hand: hold BOOT (B), tap RESET (R), release BOOT — then click Connect.

recovery.when: You’re not on Chrome, Edge, or another Chromium browser
recovery.do: Web Serial only exists there. Use the guided PlatformIO / Arduino path instead — same result, a few more steps.
